subject: Leadership hotlist: OKR check-ins & QBR prep (week of Aug 11)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: exec-distro@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-11T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Leadership hotlist: OKR check-ins & QBR prep (week of Aug 11)

Morning team — quick weekly hotlist ahead of next week's QBR dry runs. Kept this to one page (attached) and a short set of asks.

Wins
- Pilot: Dedicated pool for Retail POC reached 1k qps stable under load test (infra + autoscaler tuned) — ops/infra win, reduces unit-cost risk.
- Eval: Semantic reranker for search improved top-1 relevancy by +6 pts on the benchmark set.

Risks / Headwinds
- Model infra: GPU node preemption rate spiked 15% last 72h in us-west-2 — if sustained, latency SLOs for Dedicated customers will be impacted. Jonas is on mitigation, but we should expect a shortfall risk for next 10% of committed traffic.
- QBR-ready artifacts: We still need a cleaned runbook for the incident scenario we committed to share with Procurement (Acme). Current draft has gaps on rollback steps.

Asks (short)
1) Jonas: draft rollback runbook + mitigation ETA by EOD Thursday so we can include in Acme compliance packet.
2) Laura: can you approve a one-off QBR slot extension (+15 mins) for the Retail POC demo? We need the extra time to show latency vs. cost tradeoffs.
3) Vanessa: please surface any late exec asks from CS or Sales by Wednesday noon so we can bake into the deck.

Logistics
- Attached: 2026_Q3_hotlist_slide_deck.pdf (single-slide hotlist) and qbr_action_register.xlsx (action tracker).
- Dry-run schedule: Aug 17 (leadership preview) and Aug 18 (wider QBR). I will run the preview at 9:00am PT on the 17th.

Thanks — short and actionable.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: 2026_Q3_hotlist_slide_deck.pdf (1.2MB)
Attachment stub: qbr_action_register.xlsx (24KB)

Subject: Re: Leadership hotlist: OKR check-ins & QBR prep (week of Aug 11)

Thanks Soojin — concise and helpful.

Quick notes:
- Approved: +15min for the Retail POC demo. Please update the run of show and share with me latest by Friday.
- Hiring highlight: We have candidate slate for the Head of Product Ops; interview loop completes Friday. If this closes, it reduces a cross-org blocker on OKR delivery — I will call out in the preview.

On the Acme runbook gap: can we add a simple table that maps rollback -> owner -> exact command? Procurement needs that level of specificity. Jonas, can you confirm you can provide that by EOD Thursday (Soojin asked)?

On the preemption spike: if this is transient, we can note it as monitored; if not, we should include a short statement on fallback routing for Dedicated customers (i.e., automatic routing to spared capacity in us-east).

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Chief Operating Officer
Redwood Inference

Adding a quick update on the preemption issue and the runbook ask.

Preemption root cause: AWS capacity reclaiming older spot instances due to a new batch allocation; observed across a small subset of p4d-like pools only in us-west-2. We're shifting critical Dedicated workloads to reserved-backed spare pools (us-east-1) and enabling short-lived fallback replicas to keep tail latency within SLO. That shift is staged and will finish by EOD Thursday.

Runbook: attaching a short rollback matrix with exact commands and owners. This is intentionally terse for Procurement. If Procurement wants more, we can provide the safe-mode playbook in a follow-up.

Attachment stub: rollback_matrix_v1.docx (6KB)

Jonas
Staff Engineering, Infra
Redwood Inference
